ranges.source: GolfDB (McNally et al., CVPRW 2019) - p10-p90 of n=1399 hand-annotated tour swings from 246 PGA/LPGA/Champions Tour golfers; replaces the Tour Tempo (Novosel, 2004) 2.7-3.3 estimate, whose floor it confirms but whose ceiling captured only the lower third of the tour distribution (p50 3.39). Derived from event labels only, no video; see benchmarks/golfdb_v1.json and ADR-012

GolfDB (McNally et al., CVPRW 2019) - p90 of n=458 face-on tour swings from 122 golfers, measured by MediaPipe Pose lite at GolfDB's hand-annotated instants; one-sided (lower is better), replacing the 0.5 uncalibrated estimate. Metric definitions v3 (ear midpoint, not nose; address endpoint and shoulder-width ruler read from a short window ending at the address boundary, not the whole ADDRESS phase, which began at frame 0 - this moved p90 from 0.42 to 0.43). Unaffected by the 160x160 pixel-aspect correction, which cancels for an x-distance over an x-scale; see benchmarks/golfdb_v1.json, docs/M4_POSE_BAKEOFF.md, ADR-012 and ADR-013

GolfDB (McNally et al., CVPRW 2019) - p90 of n=458 face-on tour swings from 122 golfers, measured by MediaPipe Pose lite at GolfDB's hand-annotated instants; one-sided (lower is better), replacing the 0.6 uncalibrated estimate. Metric definitions v3 (p90 of hip drift, not max; hip visibility gate 0.7; shoulder-width ruler read from a short window ending at the address boundary, not the whole ADDRESS phase - this moved p90 from 0.28 to 0.29). Includes the 160x160 pixel-aspect correction, which moves p90 from 0.30 to 0.28; see benchmarks/golfdb_v1.json, docs/M4_POSE_BAKEOFF.md, ADR-012 and ADR-013

GolfDB (McNally et al., CVPRW 2019) - p10-p90 of n=458 face-on tour swings from 122 golfers, measured by MediaPipe Pose lite at GolfDB's hand-annotated instants. TWO-SIDED, unlike head_sway_norm and finish_balance_norm, and deliberately: 'less is better' is NOT established for lateral hip travel, because some of it is the weight shift a swing needs (recorded when career-mode step 5 refused this metric a bias finding for exactly this reason). The tour population agrees - p10 is 0.14, so 90% of tour swings show MORE hip travel than that, which is not the shape of a quantity golfers should minimise. The lower edge is assertable because it clears the instrument: tune_spatial_metric.py puts this metric's noise+boundary error at 0.050, and 0.14 sits 2.8x that above zero. REVISITED 2026-08-18 and KEPT, with the error bar that was missing from the line above: 458 clips from 122 golfers are not 458 independent samples - several clips are often cut from one broadcast of one swing - and tune_joint_structure.py's player-clustered bootstrap widens p10's 95% interval down to 0.0801. That is uncertainty about WHERE the edge belongs, not about whether the instrument resolves it: the 2.8x is a resolution claim and clustering does not touch it, while 0.1414 remains the point estimate. Do not read 0.0801 as a second hip_shift_at_top_norm, whose edge was dropped because its p10 sits BELOW its error floor; that is a different finding and its precedent does not apply here. What would reopen this: bay footage measuring near the edge, or a re-derivation over a corpus with more distinct golfers. Metric definitions v3; see benchmarks/golfdb_v1.json, ADR-010 addenda 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-18, ADR-012

GolfDB (McNally et al., CVPRW 2019) - p90 of n=458 face-on tour swings from 122 golfers, measured by MediaPipe Pose lite at GolfDB's hand-annotated instants. One-sided, and for a different reason than head_sway_norm's: not because less is better - that is unestablished here too - but because the lower edge is UNMEASURABLE. The p10 is 0.015 while tune_spatial_metric.py puts this metric's noise+boundary error at 0.053, so a low edge there would separate golfers this pipeline cannot tell apart. Only overshoot is judged, which is the half the instrument can resolve: a hip slide past the tour p90 going back is the recognised 'sway off the ball'. Metric definitions v3; see benchmarks/golfdb_v1.json, ADR-010 addendum 2026-08-12, ADR-012

GolfDB (McNally et al., CVPRW 2019) - p10-p90 of n=458 face-on tour swings from 122 golfers, measured by MediaPipe Pose lite at GolfDB's hand-annotated instants. Negative because the band lives in the RIGHT-HANDED CAMERA FRAME: more negative means the head finished further behind the hips than it started, which is what a tour swing does. evaluate_head_stays_back normalizes a left-handed golfer onto this frame before scoring, using Golfer.handedness; the corpus was normalized the same way by derive_reference.py, which resolves each subject's handedness from the sign of head_hip_offset_impact_norm (4 of 122 subjects fold, and two of them are Mickelson and Watson - the check this has instead of a handedness column). TWO-SIDED: both edges clear the instrument, tune_spatial_metric.py putting noise+boundary at 0.080 against 0.269 from p50 to either edge (3.4x). This metric is the DELTA, not the absolute head-hip offset at impact, and that is the whole point - check_metric_transfer.py found our bay clips disagree with this corpus by 0.32 shoulder-widths AT ADDRESS, before the swing starts and 4x the error, so the absolute carries a static camera bias (yaw converts head/hip depth into apparent offset, and shoulder-width normalization does not remove it). Differencing two instants under one shared address-window ruler cancels that term and leaves what the swing produced. Metric definitions v3; see benchmarks/golfdb_v1.json, ADR-010 addendum 2026-08-12, ADR-012
